history.title: History of Tanay
history.charteredDesc: Every November, Tanay celebrates the Hane Festival, a vibrant cultural and eco-tourism event honoring the town’s founding anniversary. It showcases local traditions, agricultural products, and natural attractions, while reflecting the Tanay expression “hane,” symbolizing community pride and identity.
history.elevationDesc: Tanay is known as the Adventure Capital of Rizal due to its rich natural landscapes featuring mountains, rivers, waterfalls, and forests. It offers popular outdoor activities such as hiking, camping, trekking, and sightseeing, making it a top destination for nature lovers and adventure seekers near Metro Manila.

precolonial.title: Early Settlements
precolonial.text: Tanay was originally inhabited by indigenous groups like the Dumagat. Early communities lived near rivers and forests, relying on fishing, hunting, and simple farming.

spanish.title: Spanish Colonization
spanish.text: Tanay was established as a settlement under Spanish missionaries and later became an independent town, influenced by Catholic traditions and colonial rule.

relocation.title: Town Relocation
relocation.text: Due to frequent flooding, the town was moved to its present location. During this time, the San Ildefonso de Toledo Parish Church was built, becoming a key landmark.

revolution.title: Philippine Revolution
revolution.text: Tanay joined the fight against Spain during the Philippine Revolution, supporting the Katipunan movement for independence.

american.title: American Administration
american.text: Tanay became part of Rizal. Public education, roads, and governance systems were improved under American rule.

ww2.title: World War II
ww2.text: During World War II, Tanay was occupied by Japanese forces. Guerrilla fighters operated in nearby mountains, resisting the occupation.

present.title: Modern Tanay
present.text: Today, Tanay is known for tourism and nature spots like Daranak Falls and Regina RICA, making it a popular destination.
